objectives: Calculate the power of a hydro plant from its head, flow and efficiency
Identify which turbine suits a site from its head and flow
Explain the difference between run-of-river plants, storage dams and pumped storage

questions.prompt: A mountain plant has a net head of 250 m and passes 40 m³/s at 90 % efficiency. What electrical power does it make (ρ = 1,000 kg/m³, g = 9.81 m/s²)?
questions.explain: P = 0.9 × 1,000 × 9.81 × 40 × 250 ≈ 88 million watts, or 88 MW. 98 MW forgets the 90 % efficiency, and 88 kW forgets that each cubic metre of water has a mass of 1,000 kg.

questions.prompt: Why does a hydro plant turn about 90 % of the water's energy into electricity, while fuel-burning plants manage far less?
choices: Falling water drives the turbine directly, with no heat engine and its ceiling in between
Water is denser than steam, so it carries more energy through the turbine each second
Dams store water, so the turbine can run at its most efficient speed all year
Friction heats the falling water, and the turbine recovers that heat as well
questions.explain: Falling water spins the turbine directly, so only friction and electrical losses get in the way. A fuel-burning plant must first make heat, and heat-engine physics limits how much of any heat can become work; water's density changes how much power a plant makes, not what share of the energy it keeps.

questions.prompt: Engineers are planning a mountain plant with a head of about 800 m and a small flow. Which turbine should they choose?
choices: Kaplan, because its blades swivel to match the flow
Francis, because water spirals in and it suits most large dams
Pelton, because jets of fast water striking cups suit very high heads
Kaplan or Francis equally, since the power depends only on head times flow
questions.explain: Very high heads with small flows are Pelton country: after an 800 m fall the water leaves the nozzle at well over 100 m/s, and the cups turn that speed into work. Francis runners suit heads of about 40 to 600 m and Kaplans low heads with big flows; the power equation is the same for every turbine, but each runner works well only in its own range of head.

questions.prompt: What does a pumped-storage plant do for a grid?
choices: It makes extra renewable electricity from a second river
It raises a river's flow so a run-of-river plant can run all year
It gives back more electricity than it uses, because water falls faster than it is pumped
It stores surplus electricity by pumping water uphill and returns it later, minus losses
questions.explain: Pumped storage stores energy rather than making it: when power is plentiful its machines run backwards as pumps, and when power is scarce the water runs back down through them as turbines. Like any store, it gives back less than it took in.
